name: Data Science exam (Mendeley sf3kvjwknt)
subject: Data Science
subjectiveQuestions: Evaluation Case Study: A model (M1) achieves 99% accuracy on the training set but only 30% accuracy on the testing set. What is happening to this model?
List and elucidate two major challenges in Machine Learning.
List any two major real-world applications of Data Science.
Distinguish between Structured and Semi-structured data.
Describe methods used to detect and handle outliers in a dataset.
Why is Data Normalization required for the K-Nearest Neighbors (K-NN) algorithm?
How are continuous attributes discretized? Give an example.
What does the 'K' represent in the K-Means clustering algorithm?
Name three common Hyperparameters in Machine Learning algorithms.
Classifier Comparison: Compare three SVM classifiers based on their margins and boundaries.
Explain how the Radial Basis Function (RBF) Kernel works in SVM.

key_concepts: model is trained on labeled data
learns from known inputs and outputs to make predictions
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: A type of ML where the model is trained on labeled data with known inputs and outputs.

key_concepts: identifies the problem as overfitting
model memorised training data and fails to generalise to new/test data
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: Overfitting; the model has memorized the training data but failed to generalize.

key_concepts: a statistical method / process
estimates the relationship between a dependent and independent variable(s)
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: A statistical process for estimating the relationships between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables.

key_concepts: names and explains one valid machine-learning challenge
names and explains a second, different valid challenge
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: Data quality/missing values, overfitting/underfitting, data collection, or time consumption.

key_concepts: one valid real-world application of data science
a second, different valid application
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: Healthcare/disease prediction, Finance/fraud detection, E-commerce recommendation systems.

key_concepts: structured data is organised in rows/columns or tables (e.g. SQL, Excel, CSV)
semi-structured data has tags/markers but no fixed table form (e.g. JSON, XML, HTML)
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: Structured is organized in rows/columns (SQL, Excel); Semi-structured has some markers but isn't in a grid (JSON, XML, HTML).

key_concepts: a method to detect outliers (e.g. Z-score, IQR, box or scatter plot)
a method to handle outliers (e.g. trimming, capping, imputation)
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: Detection: Z-score, IQR, Scatter plots, Box plots. Handling: Trimming, Capping, or Imputation.

key_concepts: cleaning raw data (missing, incorrect or noisy values)
transforming data into a form suitable for a model
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: The steps taken to clean and transform raw data into a format suitable for a machine learning model.

key_concepts: K-NN relies on distances between points
features with larger scales dominate the distance unless normalised
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: K-NN is distance-based; features with larger scales will dominate the distance calculation if not normalized.

key_concepts: continuous values are grouped into bins / intervals
gives a valid example of discretisation
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: By grouping values into bins or intervals, e.g., turning ages 1-100 into 'Child,' 'Adult,' 'Senior.'

key_concepts: K is the number of clusters
K is chosen / fixed beforehand
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: The predefined number of clusters or groups the data will be divided into.

key_concepts: names at least two valid hyperparameters
names a third valid hyperparameter
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: K in K-NN, Learning Rate, Number of Estimators/Trees, Max Depth, or Batch Size.

key_concepts: an optimisation algorithm that minimises a cost / loss function
iteratively updates parameters in the direction of steepest descent (negative gradient)
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: An optimization algorithm used to minimize the cost function by iteratively moving toward the steepest descent.

key_concepts: compares the classifiers by margin width (wider margin is better)
considers whether data points fall inside the margin / gutter
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: Discussion on maximizing the margin and ensuring no data points fall within the 'gutter' or margin.

key_concepts: maps data into a higher-dimensional space
allows a non-linear decision boundary
subjectiveRubrics.model_answer: It transforms data into a higher-dimensional space to find a non-linear decision boundary.
